title: Generating and Predicting Output Perturbations in Image Segmenters
problem: Image segmentation DNN and transformer models used in safety-critical autonomous pipelines are vulnerable to imperceptible sensor noise that causes corrupted segmentation outputs, threatening system safety.
motivation: Image segmentation is core safety component in autonomous systems, but robustness to adversarial input perturbations inadequately understood for modern transformer-based and CNN segmenters.
method: Uses genetic algorithms to generate adversarial noise patterns that induce segmentation corruption. Proposes novel ML model to predict whether input image will yield corrupted output from noise, achieving >96% prediction accuracy. Evaluates on YOLOv8 and DETR segmenters.
key_novelty: First corruption prediction model for image segmentation with >96% accuracy; demonstrates generation of imperceptible adversarial noise unrelated to corrupted image regions.
contributions: Genetic algorithm-based adversarial noise generation method for image segmentation
Corruption prediction model achieving >96% accuracy on real segmenters
Evaluation on state-of-the-art segmenters (YOLOv8, DETR) demonstrating imperceptible yet effective attacks
limitations: Evaluation limited to two model architectures; transferability across different segmentation architectures not explored.
primary_theme: adversarial noise generation and corruption prediction for vision safety
